title: Four Workers Die After Fall at TSMC Building Site in Kaohsiung
summaryZh: 台積電高雄廠工地墜落意外增至4死，鋼構吊掛暫停，團體要求獨立監督。
summaryHi: काओशुंग में TSMC निर्माण स्थल पर गिरने से चार मज़दूरों की मौत, काम रोका गया।
summaryEs: Mueren cuatro obreros tras una caída en una obra de TSMC en Kaohsiung.
summaryJa: TSMC高雄工場の建設現場で転落事故、死者4人に。鉄骨作業を停止。
summaryKo: TSMC 가오슝 공장 건설 현장 추락 사고로 4명 사망, 철골 작업 중단.
summaryEn: A fourth worker has died after a fall at TSMC's Kaohsiung site, and steel work is halted.
paragraphs: The death toll from a construction accident at a TSMC chip plant in Kaohsiung has risen to four, after another worker died in hospital on Wednesday, according to the Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau.

The four men fell several storeys on Tuesday while working on Fab 22, a factory that the chip giant is building in the southern city. The exact cause of the fall is still under investigation, and penalties will depend on what investigators find and on Taiwan's workplace safety laws.

The lifting of steel beams at the site has been suspended. It can only restart once Shang Hao Machinery Co., the firm that employed the four workers, submits an improvement plan that passes a review. The site had received three labour inspections last year and 18 so far this year, and two other contractors were fined a combined NT$210,000 (about US$6,500) after a check in July.
TSMC said it had voluntarily halted steel structure work at the Kaohsiung site and at all its other new plants under construction in Taiwan, and that it was helping with the investigation.
The Taiwan Association for Victims of Occupational Injuries urged the company to carry out safety checks at every site and to set up independent, third-party oversight that includes workers.
There was a bad accident at a building site in Kaohsiung, in the south of Taiwan. The company TSMC is building a new chip factory there.
On Tuesday, four workers fell from a high place. On Wednesday, the fourth man died in hospital. Now all four workers are dead.
The four men worked for a small company, Shang Hao Machinery. People are still trying to find out why the accident happened.
For now, workers cannot lift steel at the site. The company must write a plan to make the work safer first.
TSMC also stopped steel work at all its new building sites in Taiwan. A group for hurt workers says TSMC must check safety at every site.
A fourth worker has died after a serious accident at a building site for TSMC, Taiwan's biggest chip maker, in the southern city of Kaohsiung.

The workers fell several floors on Tuesday at TSMC's new factory, called Fab 22, which is still being built. The fourth man died of his injuries in hospital on Wednesday, the Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau said.

The cause of the accident is still being investigated. All lifting of steel beams at the site has stopped. Work can only start again after Shang Hao Machinery, the company that employed the four men, gives an improvement plan and it is approved.
Inspectors had already checked the site 18 times this year. In July, two other companies there were fined a total of NT$210,000.

TSMC said it had stopped steel work at all its new factory sites in Taiwan and was helping the investigation. A group that supports injured workers asked TSMC to check every site and to let an independent group watch over safety.

A fourth worker has died following a fall at a TSMC construction site in Kaohsiung, raising fresh questions about safety standards on the projects that underpin Taiwan's booming chip industry.

The men plunged several storeys on Tuesday while working on Fab 22, the semiconductor giant's new plant in the southern city. The latest victim succumbed to his injuries in hospital on Wednesday, the Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau confirmed. Investigators have yet to establish the cause, and any penalties will be determined under occupational safety legislation.

In the meantime, all lifting of steel beams at the site has been suspended. Work will resume only once Shang Hao Machinery Co., which employed the four victims, submits an improvement plan that clears official review. Notably, the site had already been inspected 18 times this year, and two other contractors were fined a combined NT$210,000 after a steel structure check in July.
TSMC said it had voluntarily paused steel structure work not only in Kaohsiung but at all its new fabs under construction across Taiwan, and was cooperating with investigators and subcontractors.

A victims' advocacy group went further, urging investors and government representatives to press TSMC to disclose its accident analysis and to establish independent oversight in which workers have a genuine voice.
The number of fatalities from a construction accident at a TSMC site in Kaohsiung has risen to four, prompting renewed scrutiny of safety practices behind Taiwan's rapid expansion of chip production.

The workers fell several storeys on Tuesday at Fab 22, a plant still under construction, and the fourth victim died in hospital on Wednesday. According to the Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau, the precise cause remains under investigation, and any penalties will be imposed in accordance with occupational safety regulations.

Authorities have suspended the lifting of steel beams at the site. Operations may resume only after Shang Hao Machinery Co., the subcontractor that employed the men, submits an improvement plan that is subsequently approved. Significantly, the site had been inspected 18 times this year, and two other contractors had already been fined a total of NT$210,000.
TSMC responded by voluntarily halting steel structure work at all of its new plants under construction in Taiwan, stating that it was cooperating fully with the investigation.

Nevertheless, a group representing victims of workplace injuries argues that such measures are insufficient. It has called for comprehensive inspections, greater transparency about accident analysis and an independent oversight mechanism involving workers, arguing that accident prevention should be part of how managers are assessed.
